claims.text: Brand inclusions restrict a Search campaign so it only serves on queries tied to brands you choose. They are not available for Performance Max, which is the easy mistake to make.

claims.text: It is a control, not a signal: it limits where the campaign can serve. Google recommends using brand settings only on campaigns that really need them, so you do not cut off conversion opportunities.

claims.text: Create a brand list at account level, adding the brands you want. If a brand is missing from the library, request it be added.

claims.text: Apply the brand list as an inclusion to your Search campaign. Do this on a Search campaign, not Performance Max.

claims.text: Conversion rate and CPA: if your Search campaign was spending on queries unrelated to the brands you sell, limiting it to chosen brands may raise conversion rate and lower CPA. The trade-off is lower impression volume and fewer conversion opportunities. Results are not guaranteed.

claims.text: Impression share and total conversions: because the campaign serves only on selected brand queries, volume may fall if the list is narrow or incomplete. Check these metrics against your goals before and after applying it.
